description: lib.rs lines 211-215 (check_revocation doc): the important caveat that Ok(()) can mean either 'not revoked' OR 'not covered by this CRL' is explained in the body of the CrlChecker struct doc (lib.rs lines 59-70) and partially in the trait doc, but the trait method's own doc comment only has a short 'dual semantics' note in the tail. Callers implementing the RevocationChecker trait or using it generically will read the trait-method doc first; the full explanation lives on the struct. Hard-fail callers may miss this and incorrectly treat Ok(()) as a definitive 'not revoked' signal. Suggested fix: promote the dual-semantics warning to a NOTE: or # Security admonition at the top of the check_revocation doc comment on the trait, not just in the CrlChecker struct-level doc.
title: P3: lib.rs doc comment: 'Ok(()) dual semantics' warning is buried
